questions.question: What changes about useState, useReducer, and Context when moving from web React to React Native?
options: They all require a different import path with different behavior
Nothing — they work identically, since React Native runs the same React reconciliation and hook rules
useReducer is not supported in React Native
Context causes a full app re-render in React Native, unlike on the web
questions.explanation: The core React programming model is unchanged between web and native — only the host components and platform APIs (like storage) differ.

questions.question: Why can't AsyncStorage be read synchronously inside a useState initializer, the way the web course's useLocalStorage reads localStorage?
options: AsyncStorage's I/O is asynchronous (always returns a Promise) since native storage access can't block the JS thread the way localStorage can block the web main thread
useState initializers cannot run any code at all
There's no actual difference, the same pattern works unchanged
questions.explanation: Because every AsyncStorage method returns a Promise, reading it has to happen in an effect (after mount), not synchronously during initial state computation.

questions.question: What data types can be stored directly in AsyncStorage?
options: Any JavaScript value, including functions and class instances
Only strings — non-string values must be serialized with JSON.stringify before storing and parsed back with JSON.parse after reading
questions.explanation: Like localStorage on the web, AsyncStorage is a string-only key-value store, so structured data needs manual JSON serialization.

questions.question: Why does `useAsyncStorage` return a `loaded` flag that `useLocalStorage` on the web doesn't need?
options: It's an arbitrary addition with no functional purpose
Because the restored value now arrives asynchronously, callers need a way to distinguish 'still the initial placeholder' from 'the real restored value'
loaded is required by the AsyncStorage API itself
It makes the hook's return value serializable
questions.explanation: Since reading is no longer synchronous, something has to signal when the real value has actually arrived — otherwise the UI might flash the default/placeholder value briefly on every app launch.
